[Performance][Worker] Reuse V2 attention metadata across cache groups and batch GDN state writes (#20345)

### What this PR does / why we need it?

Model Runner V2 builds the same request layout repeatedly when a hybrid
model has several compatible GDN cache groups. The Mamba model state now
builds one layout per cache spec and builder type. Each remaining group
binds its own physical state indices and batches writes to its captured
graph buffers. A repeated decode layout refreshes its inputs for the
current step.

Checkpoint-enabled groups build independently because each group can
reserve a different physical page. Builders with a step hook still
receive the complete layer map. Hybrid MTP support for FA3 is tracked in
#23347.

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

Compatible GDN groups use the optimization automatically. The gain
depends on the number of groups and how much of metadata preparation
lies on the critical path.

### How was this patch tested?

Tested `c6d8eef27` against `4f49ae332` on the same A3 with Qwen3.5-9B
BF16, DFlash with seven draft tokens, TP1, colocated prefill/decode and
full decode graphs. Every request used 16,384 input tokens and generated
256 tokens. Each cell reports mean time per output token across two runs
after warmup.

| Concurrent requests | Baseline TPOT | PR TPOT | Reduction |
| ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 1 | 5.787 ms | 3.829 ms | 33.8% |
| 4 | 6.941 ms | 4.836 ms | 30.3% |

All 10 paired outputs matched the baseline token for token. In a
separate instrumented run at concurrency 1, both revisions took 34
target iterations. Full GDN builds fell from 816 to 34, with 782
group-local updates. At concurrency 4, 35 iterations went from 840 full
builds to 35, with 805 updates.

746 unit tests and 29 NPU operator and graph cases passed on A3. These
cover group-local checkpoint offsets, strided inputs, padding, and
group-specific buffer addresses across graph replay. The final split
revision has been benchmarked on A3.

pytest -q tests/ut/ops/test_gdn_{attn_builder,aligned_indices,graph_state}.py \
  tests/ut/worker/test_{model_runner_v2_mamba,attn_utils_v2,v2_dummy_padding,mamba_aligned_views}.py

[CI] Exclude comment-only patch/__init__.py from src paths-filter (#23519)

### What this PR does / why we need it?

`vllm_ascend/patch/__init__.py` is a comment-only patch catalog with no
executable code. Currently it matches `vllm_ascend/**` under the `src`
paths-filter, forcing comment-only patch catalog cleanup PRs (such as
#23278) to require test labels and run CPU UT / precision test
selection.

This PR adds `- '!vllm_ascend/patch/__init__.py'` under the `src` filter
in:
- `.github/workflows/pr_test.yaml`
- `.github/workflows/_selected_tests.yaml` (mirrored `src` filter)

Because `dorny/paths-filter@v4` uses `predicate-quantifier:
some-with-excludes`:
- PRs touching **only** `vllm_ascend/patch/__init__.py` (without a
test-enabling label) resolve `src=false` and skip `cpu-ut` /
`select-tests` / E2E while still running `pre-commit` and `ci-gate`
(including CODEOWNERS).
- PRs touching `vllm_ascend/patch/__init__.py` alongside any real source
file still resolve `src=true`.

[BugFix][HiSparse] Bound MemCache Device GET batches (#23442)

### What this PR does / why we need it?

MemCache acquires a read lease for both Host and Device bulk GETs. The
HiSparse AscendStore path applied its 256 MiB batch budget only to Host
reads. On A5 TP8 with a near-1M GLM-5.3 prefix, each rank submitted all
8,183 C8 Indexer keys in one Device GET. The SDK returned `-3106` after
the read lease expired and the replay returned HTTP 500.

Apply the existing 256 MiB budget to both directions on the registered
HiSparse path. Keep single keys intact and preserve SDK statuses across
batches.

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

Yes. Colocated HiSparse with MemCache `host_tcp` can replay long
prefixes that previously failed due to a large Device GET. No
configuration change is required. This is a follow-up to the unreleased
HiSparse/AscendStore integration in #21924.

### How was this patch tested?

- `TORCH_DEVICE_BACKEND_AUTOLOAD=0 pytest -q
tests/ut/distributed/ascend_store`: 1,315 passed, 12 skipped. The new
Device test fails with the original backend. Coverage includes both
destinations, the exact byte limit, oversized keys, and receive failure
followed by retry.
- A5 950DT, single node TP8, GLM-5.3 W4A4C8 MXFP4, MTP=3, decode graph,
MemCache 1.3.0 `host_tcp`, default 10-second lease. For hardware
validation the separate Resident DMA fix from #23336 was applied to the
test checkout. The PR contains only the GET fix and its tests.

[Feature] support direct reload for BF16 Qwen on Ascend (#22493)

### What this PR does / why we need it?

Enable direct weight reload for unquantized BF16 Qwen on Ascend over
disk checkpoints and unpacked HCCL. This lets a running rollout worker
update its weights in place and continue serving in eager mode or
replaying its captured decode graphs.

The Ascend worker retains its existing disk reload entry point.
Unquantized MoE layers reject direct reload when fused expert processing
is enabled. The online HCCL test compares alternating checkpoints
against independent cold loads.

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?
Yes. On the verified vLLM main build, users can opt in with
`VLLM_RELOAD_MODE=direct` for BF16 Qwen disk reload and unpacked HCCL
weight updates. The HCCL configuration used for validation sets
`weight_nz_mode=0`. For MoE direct reload, set `enable_fused_mc2=0`.
Fused MC2 and MegaMoE support is tracked in #23430.

### How was this patch tested?

Historical coverage of the paths in this PR on Ascend A3 (verified vLLM
`c410543d9`): ten online cases and two disk comparisons across two BF16
Qwen models. The revisions below predate the split.

| Model | Layers | TP | vLLM-Ascend revision tested | Passed |
| --- | ---: | ---: | --- | ---: |
| Qwen3-0.6B (dense) | 28 | 1 | `8f8c1a67f` | 6/6 |
| Qwen3-30B-A3B (MoE) | 48 | 2 | `de2ac238b` (before the rebase) | 6/6 |

#### Online weight reload

Each case updated A → B → A in one running server. HCCL used a separate
trainer NPU. IPC trainers shared the inference devices. Times below are
measured per update. The 30B packed IPC case ran on the same host as the
0.6B cases; the other 30B online cases ran on another A3 host.

| Model | Transport | Execution mode | A → B (s) | B → A (s) |
| --- | --- | --- | ---: | ---: |
| 0.6B | Unpacked HCCL | Dense graph | 0.57 | 0.54 |
| 0.6B | Unpacked HCCL | Eager | 0.54 | 0.54 |
| 0.6B | Packed HCCL | Dense graph | 0.71 | 0.67 |
| 0.6B | Unpacked IPC | Dense graph | 9.38 | 9.36 |
| 0.6B | Packed IPC | Dense graph | 9.35 | 9.39 |
| 30B-A3B | Unpacked HCCL | AllToAll/MC2 | 40.62 | 40.53 |
| 30B-A3B | Unpacked HCCL | Eager | 37.59 | 37.61 |
| 30B-A3B | Packed HCCL | AllToAll/MC2 | 7.56 | 48.19 |
| 30B-A3B | Unpacked IPC | AllToAll/MC2 | 155.53 | 109.20 |
| 30B-A3B | Packed IPC | AllToAll/MC2 | 17.75 | 17.80 |

After each update, token IDs and top-5 logprobs matched an independent
cold load of that checkpoint (absolute tolerance `1e-4` for logprobs).
Both models retained runtime weight addresses and layouts. Graph cases
replayed their captured decode graphs with zero recaptures, eager cases
recorded zero replays, and every case passed the final HTTP generation
check.

#### Disk reload comparison

Each mode reloaded checkpoint A under `FULL_DECODE_ONLY` once for
warm-up and three more times for measurement. Values are medians over
the three measured rounds.

| Model | Mode | Temporary tensor estimate per rank (MiB) | Total
temporary tensor estimate (MiB) | Reload time (s) | Sampled peak HBM
across inference NPUs (GiB) |
| --- | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 0.6B | Layerwise | 296.8 | 296.8 | 0.202 | 2.576 |
| 0.6B | Direct | 0 | 0 | 0.306 | 2.381 |
| 30B-A3B | Layerwise | 960 | 1920 | 5.241 | 63.346 |
| 30B-A3B | Direct | 384 | 768 | 3.498 | 62.215 |

Temporary tensor memory is the allocator peak minus the end-of-reload
allocation on each worker. For 0.6B, this estimate fell from 296.8 MiB
to zero at TP1, while median reload time increased from 0.202 s to 0.306
s. For 30B-A3B at TP2, direct reload reduced the estimate from 960 to
384 MiB per rank (60%) and reduced median time from 5.241 s to 3.498 s.
Device HBM is sampled separately by summing device usage at each sample
and taking the largest sum in the reload window.

commits.message:
[Performance] Dispatch small-batch single-group DSA o_proj wo_a to the plain 2D matmul (#21782)

### What this PR does / why we need it?
DeepSeek-V4(-V4.1) DSA o\_proj low-rank projection `wo_a` is always
dispatched to `npu_transpose_batchmatmul` on a 3D weight of shape
`[n_local_groups, hidden_size, o_lora_rank]`. When all o\_groups land on
the current TP rank (`n_local_groups == config.o_groups // tp_size ==
1`, e.g. TP8 for DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash), the batched-transpose path
degenerates to a plain linear but still pays a large fixed kernel cost
at decode batch sizes (M << N).

Production decode trace (DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash W4A8 TP8/EP8, bs=2):
`aclnnTransposeBatchMatMul` 40 calls/step x \~50.6 us = **2.03 ms/step**
(\~10% of the 5.3 us/call HBM floor of the 8.4 MB bf16 weight).
Op-level microbench on the same per-rank weight ([K=4096, N=1024] bf16,
ND):
num_tokens | npu_transpose_batchmatmul | plain 2D matmul
-- | -- | --
8 (decode) | 43–50 us (run-dependent) | ~20 us
128 | ~45 us | ~20 us
3500 (prefill chunk) | ~122 us device (production trace) | ~121 us
device

This PR dispatches `_wo_a_bmm` to a plain `torch.matmul` when
`n_local_groups == 1`, the weight is unquantized (no `weight_scale`),
and `num_tokens <= 128`: the 3D ND weight is `[1, K, N]` contiguous, so
the 2D operand is a free `view(K, N)`. **prefill is untouched**. The
weight layout, weight loading, and RL weight-switch paths are unchanged.

**Scope**: the decode speedup applies only to deployments where all
o\_groups land on one rank (`n_local_groups == 1`, i.e. attention TP
size >= o\_groups, e.g. a colocated TP8/EP8 serving of
DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash). In P/D-disaggregated deployments where decode
scales out with large EP while attention TP stays small (`n_local_groups
> 1`), the dispatch condition is not met and `_wo_a_bmm` keeps the
original transpose-batchmatmul path — for those configurations this
patch is a no-op: no benefit, but also no behavior or performance
change.

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?
No API or config change. The projection math is identical (same GEMM,
different kernel selection); outputs may differ at bf16 rounding level
as with any kernel change.

### How was this patch tested?

- Serving benchmark (910B, vllm bench serve, DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-1017
W4A8, TP=8, DP=1, random 3500 input / 46500 prefix / 350 output, conc 6,
no MTP, 2 runs per side):

metric | baseline | patched | delta
--- | --- | --- | ---
TPOT mean (ms) | 31.24 / 31.31 | 29.90 / 30.02 | -4.2%
TPOT median (ms) | 30.85 / 30.94 | 29.57 / 29.57 | -4.3%
ITL median (ms) | 28.47 / 28.58 | 27.16 / 27.24 | -4.7%
Output tok/s | 155.6 / 154.9 | 160.9 / 160.3 | +3.5%
E2EL median (ms) | 12982 / 13048 | 12537 / 12601 | -3.4%
TTFT median (ms) | 2219 / 2273 | 2262 / 2247 | unchanged

The TPOT delta (-1.31 ms) matches the device accounting: the 40 wo\_a
calls/step drop from \~50.6 us (transpose kernel) to \~18 us (plain
matmul). TTFT median and P99 are unchanged, confirming prefill is
untouched by the threshold dispatch.

commits.message:
[Feature] support MLA attention mode for Kimi-K3.1 DFlash2 draft models (#21675)

Checkpoints such as RadixArk/Kimi-K3.1-Dflash2-Preview declare
`dflash_config.attention_mode="mla"` and store DeepSeek-style MLA draft
weights
(`q_a_proj`/`kv_a_proj_with_mqa`/`kv_a_layernorm`/`kv_b_proj`/`q_b_proj`/`o_proj`),
which the GQA-only `DFlash2Qwen3Attention` cannot load. All five draft
layers of this checkpoint also keep a **1024-token sliding window**,
which the Ascend MLA path previously dropped before it reached the
attention kernel, silently corrupting long-context drafts.

This PR makes the checkpoint serve end-to-end on Ascend and makes the
draft's sliding window actually enforced in decode attention on the
verified TP-only configuration.

### What this PR does / why we need it?

**MLA attention mode** (the original scope):
- Add `DFlash2Qwen3MLADecoderLayer` built on `AscendKimiMLAAttention`,
the same MLA draft attention already used by the Kimi K3 DSpark draft.
- Add `DFlash2Qwen3MLAModel`: extends the stacked weight mapper to fuse
the separate A-projections into `fused_qkv_a_proj`, and writes context
KV into the MLA latent cache via the Ascend MLA prolog/prefill writers.
- Dispatch on `dflash_config.attention_mode` in
`DFlash2Qwen3ForCausalLM` so the existing `DFlash2DraftModel`
registration covers both GQA and MLA drafts.
- Make `get_draft_kv_cache_layer_names`/`get_draft_attn_causal` tolerate
MLA attention modules.

**Sliding-window enforcement** (the acceptance-rate fix):
- Resolve the per-layer window exactly like upstream
`_resolve_layer_attention`: `dflash_config.use_swa` forces SWA on every
layer (even an all-full `layer_types`); otherwise only
`sliding_attention` layers are windowed, with the size from
`dflash_config.swa_window_size` or the top-level `sliding_window`. The
top-level `use_sliding_window`/`max_window_layers` pair is intentionally
not consulted — upstream ignores it, and the resolution must agree with
the attention layers upstream builds from the same config. Like
upstream, a sliding layer without any configured window size raises
`ValueError` at load time instead of silently running window-free; a
zero window passes through as configured.
- The registered Ascend Kimi wrapper forwards the resolved layer window
to `MLAAttention` during construction. The backend selector and MLA
implementation see the same window.
- For a causal window of `W` tokens, the kernel can read the current
token and its `W-1` predecessors. On A3, eligible Kimi K3.1 DFlash2
drafts reuse the device-side MLA tiling from #23221. Both
`get_scheduler_metadata` and `flash_attn_with_kvcache` receive
`causal=True` and `window_size=(W-1, 0)`.
- The A3 path requires a uniform causal MLA window and `flash-attn-npu
>= 0.5.1.post1` with the split-query MLA operators. Eligible A5 drafts
use FlashMLA BAND with `mask_mode=4`, `win_left=W-1`, and `win_right=0`.
Other supported windowed layers use FIA V2 with `sparse_mode=4`,
`pre_tokens=W-1`, and `next_tokens=0`.
- Draft KV cache intentionally keeps full retention for now: DFlash
context precompute writes every context row, so a window-limited cache
would leave rows unread by the windowed decode path but still visible to
the not-yet-windowed draft prefill path. Window-limited caching is a
follow-up.
- The device-side tiling paths share one window schedule across draft
layers. In a heterogeneous draft, windowed layers use FIA and
full-attention layers retain their usual backend selection.
- Decode context parallelism (DCP) handling: DCP selects
`AscendMlaDCPImpl` for every MLA attention group, and that decode path
applies no `pre_tokens` band (`sparse_mode=0` with only the causal spec
mask), so a windowed MLA draft under DCP would silently attend the full
DCP-local KV. Such configs are refused at startup with a clear error —
the same restriction upstream vLLM #68214 encodes by refusing DCP for
windowed DFlash2 drafts. DCP support for windowed drafts is a follow-up.
- Windowed MLA drafts require causal attention. The supported band ends
at the current token, so a non-causal window is rejected at startup.

**Rejection-adjusted draft lengths.** The KV length after rejection sets
the right edge of the causal window. At the model length limit, the
per-request sample position determines how many packed query tokens
remain valid. A3 represents each clipped suffix as a zero-KV segment on
device, so later requests keep their physical token offsets. A5 passes
the valid prefix through `seqused_q`. FIA shares an exact, zero-padded
host length mirror across the metadata builds in each proposal. Padding
keeps slot `-1` in eager execution and FULL graph replay.

**Metadata build flow.** Eager execution and FULL graph replay both
enter the upstream `_build_attn_metadata` hook. The FIA-backed MLA
builder receives exact host lengths. The windowed A3 and A5 builders
read the device lengths directly. On A3, the graph manager refreshes the
captured schedule once per replay.

**Device-length scope**: the K3.1 + DFlash2 device-length fast path (no
per-step CPU length sync) currently covers the verified TP-only
configuration; pipeline parallelism, context parallelism, KV-transfer
(P/D), sparse-KV offload, and adaptive verification stay on exact host
counts, and DCP stays on exact host counts as well (the windowed-DCP
combination is refused above). The policy is registered from the Kimi
K3.1 model state via the upstream `initialize_spec_cpu_length_sync`
extension point, so the runner core stays untouched. Relaxing the gate
to those configurations is a follow-up.

**Aux hidden stream contract** (training/serving alignment):
- `fix(kimi_k3)`: capture the materialized AttnRes aux stream when the
DFlash draft declares `aux_hidden_stream="attn_res"` —
Kimi-K3.1-Dflash2-Preview declares `aux_hidden_stream="attn_res"` with
`target_layer_ids=[7, 23, 51, 67, 83, 91]`, meaning the draft was
trained consuming the AttnRes mixed value (the consumption-layer
`res_proj`/`res_norm` mixture collected at target-layer boundaries), but
Ascend only enabled the materialized capture for `method=="dspark"`, so
DFlash2 served on the residual prefix-sum instead. The contract is now
honored by enabling the AttnRes materialized capture for DFlash2 drafts
that declare it, reusing the same proven capture path as DSpark-Qwen3.
Upstream vLLM has the same AttnRes stream gated behind
`VLLM_KIMI_K3_AUX_ATTN_RES_STREAM` (default off) and never reads the
checkpoint field, so this is not a divergence from upstream — it is
honoring a checkpoint declaration that upstream also effectively ignores
by default.

**Supporting fixes**:
- `fix(kimi_k3)`: load DSA indexer weights into the Ascend indexer stack
— the upstream amd loader renames `.self_attn.indexer.*` to
`.dsa_indexer.*` before lookup, which raises `KeyError` on the first DSA
layer for any Kimi-K3.1 checkpoint with DSA layers; indexer weights
matching a registered Ascend parameter are now consumed in
`AscendKimiLinearModel.load_weights` and reported under their original
checkpoint names.
- `fix(kimi_k3)`: build target embedding on the last PP stage for
target-embed drafts (the `spec_decode_needs_target_embed` contract,
matching upstream llama behavior).
- `fix(dflash2)`: mirror upstream causality resolution exactly
(`_dflash_layer_causal`, including the checkpoint-level `is_causal` flag
that upstream consults first), so the published per-layer causality, the
draft-wide non-causal backend requirement, and the per-layer attention
flags resolved from the same config cannot disagree for any checkpoint.
GQA drafts keep the upstream per-layer resolution; the only behavior
change for existing drafts is the intentional startup refusal below.

**Startup validation for windowed MLA drafts.** Windowed MLA requires
causal attention and a decode context parallel size of one.

**Upstream relation.** This is the Ascend counterpart of
vllm-project/vllm#68214 for the Kimi K3.1 DFlash2 checkpoint. A3
windowed MLA, A5 FlashMLA BAND, and FIA apply the same causal window as
upstream sparse MLA decode.

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

Yes. `RadixArk/Kimi-K3.1-Dflash2-Preview` (and checkpoints with the same
`dflash_config.attention_mode="mla"` + sliding-window draft layers) now
load and serve on Ascend with correct draft attention on the verified
TP-only configuration. Launching a windowed MLA draft with decode
context parallelism now fails fast at startup instead of silently
dropping the window. Launching a non-causal MLA draft that declares a
sliding window now fails fast at startup instead of silently dropping
the window, and declaring a sliding window without any window size now
fails fast at load time, matching upstream validation.

### How was this patch tested?

- Unit tests added/updated under `tests/ut/` (window resolution from
config covering the upstream
`use_swa`/`swa_window_size`/`layer_types`/`sliding_window` shapes,
heterogeneous window selection, DCP refusal for windowed MLA drafts, the
non-causal window refusal, the missing-window-size error and zero-window
passthrough matching upstream, FlashMLA eligibility at layer
construction, causality resolution parity with upstream including the
`is_causal`-first order, the DFlash aux-stream contract selection
honoring `aux_hidden_stream`, rejection-adjusted host lengths with the
proposal-scoped cache, capped-window valid query prefixes, the
common-hook FULL-replay padding update for FIA-backed GQA and MLA
drafts, and the device-length policy). An A5 single-card e2e test
exercises the BAND decode path (eager and graph replay against a
sliding-window reference at the model length limit).
- On A3 with `flash-attn-npu 0.5.1.post1`, the single-card
`test_a3_dflash_mla_window_replay` checks the 1024-token window against
a reference. Three replays change the valid query counts of two requests
independently, including a fully clipped request and a padded graph row.
The focused A3 suites passed 506 tests (7 skipped). On A5, the BAND
operator and focused suites passed 344 tests against the pinned vLLM
main revision (7 skipped) and 342 against v0.34.0 (9 skipped).
- Earlier manual multi-node e2e on Ascend A5 covered the sliding-window
fix end-to-end (target Kimi-K3.1-Pro, draft Kimi-K3.1-Dflash2-Preview,
TP32, `num_speculative_tokens=7`, long-context workloads); end-to-end

[BugFix] Allow DeepSeek V4.1 DSpark MXFP8 main_proj and DSA wo_a layouts (#21953)

### What this PR does / why we need it?

DeepSeek V4.1 DSpark on a ModelSlim W8A8_MXFP8 checkpoint
(`quant_method: ascend`) built `main_proj` as BF16, so the draft loader
failed on `main_proj.scale`. DSA `wo_a` also needs an ND weight of
`[n_local_groups, hidden, o_lora_rank]` for
`npu_transpose_quant_batchmatmul`. That 3D layout is specific to
DeepSeek V4 and V4.1 and does not belong on the shared MXFP8 linear
method.

This change keeps the quantized `main_proj` contract and serves DeepSeek
V4 and V4.1 MXFP8 linears from one method:

- Read `quant_method` from the draft checkpoint `quantization_config`.
When the checkpoint does not set it, use
`vllm_config.quant_config.get_name()`.
- Pass `vllm_config.quant_config` into `main_proj` when packed-cache ops
are available and the method is `fp8` or `ascend`.
- Register the module as `mtp.0.main_proj` so per-layer quant
descriptions match the checkpoint name.
- Register both `("W8A8_MXFP8", "ds_linear")` and `("fp8", "ds_linear")`
on `AscendW8A8MXFP8DSDynamicLinearMethod`, and remove
`AscendW8A8MXFP8DSRequantizedLinearMethod`. The class stores
`quant_config.get_name()` on `quant_method` and keeps per-group scales
when that name is `ascend`. ModelSlim checkpoints keep per-group uint8
scales. Official FP8 checkpoints still expand block scales, including
32x32 and 128x128; a missing block size uses the runtime group size.
With `--quantization ascend`, every quantized linear on DeepSeek V4 or
V4.1 uses `ds_linear`. Other models stay on `linear`. ModelSlim
description files stay unchanged.
- For `wo_a` with `o_lora_rank > 0`, store ND weight `[n_local_groups,
hidden, o_lora_rank]` and scale `[n_local_groups, K/2, o_lora_rank, 2]`.
Other ModelSlim layers use the shared 2D MXFP8 post-processing. Official
FP8 `wo_a` and `wo_b` keep their post-processing after the block-scale
expansion.
- Set `weight_switch_output_gather_specs` to gather dim 0, matching
`ds_linear`, so PCP full-weight prefill reconstructs the `wo_a` groups.
This path does not restore weights for RL reload.

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

Yes. A DeepSeek V4.1 DSpark ModelSlim W8A8_MXFP8 (`ascend`) checkpoint
keeps `main_proj` quantized and can load `main_proj.scale`. FP8
`main_proj` still receives the runtime quant config when packed-cache
ops are available. With `--quantization ascend`, DeepSeek V4 and V4.1
W8A8_MXFP8 linears use `("W8A8_MXFP8", "ds_linear")`: `wo_a` is stored
as grouped ND, and PCP output gather uses dim 0. Other models keep the
shared 2D `("W8A8_MXFP8", "linear")` method. Official `--quantization
deepseek_v4_fp8` uses that same `ds_linear` class and still expands
block scales, including 32x32 and 128x128.

### How was this patch tested?

Unit tests added with the bugfix:

- `tests/ut/models/test_deepseek_v41_dspark.py`
- `test_draft_constructor_uses_upstream_head_contracts` asserts `prefix
== "mtp.0.main_proj"`.
- `test_draft_main_proj_keeps_modelslim_quant_contract` covers
`quant_method="ascend"` on the checkpoint with no runtime method, and a
runtime method of `ascend` with no checkpoint quantization config.
- `tests/ut/quantization/configs/test_modelslim_config.py`
- `test_deepseek_v4_family_mxfp8_linear_uses_ds_linear` selects
`ds_linear` for `deepseek_v4` and `deepseek_v41`, and `linear` for
another model type.
- `test_get_quant_method_for_linear` keeps a non-DeepSeek quantized
linear on `linear`.
- `tests/ut/quantization/methods/w8a8/test_w8a8_mxfp8.py`
- `test_dsa_wo_a_3d_layout` builds
`AscendW8A8MXFP8DSDynamicLinearMethod` with quant method `ascend` and
checks the ModelSlim 3D `wo_a` weight and scale shapes and values.
- `test_output_sharded_full_weight_prefill_gather` checks that the
ModelSlim DeepSeek path gathers both tensors on dim 0.
- `test_process_weights_uses_checkpoint_block_size` checks official FP8
block-scale expansion for block sizes 32 and 128.
- `test_wo_a_layout_uses_loaded_shard` checks the official FP8 `wo_a`
layout when the quant method is not ModelSlim.
- `tests/ut/quantization/methods/test_mx_weight_format_gate.py`

`AscendW8A8MXFP8DSDynamicLinearMethod((128, 128))` on both the reject

[Feature][Model] Support DeepSeek-V4.1 vision encoder ACL graphs (#21519)

### What this PR does / why we need it?

DeepSeek-V4.1 on Ascend currently encodes images through per-image eager
ViT
and aligner calls. This PR connects the model to the existing encoder
ACL graph
manager so eligible image batches can replay captured encoder execution,
reducing repeated Python dispatch and operator launch overhead.

The implementation reuses the upstream
`DeepseekV4VLEncoderCudaGraphMixin`
introduced and refined in
[vllm#56625](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/56625)
and [vllm#58499](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/58499):

- Add packed ViT execution with precomputed RoPE inputs and `cu_seqlens`
  boundaries to keep attention isolated between images.
- Add packed aligner execution using gather and masking, preserving the
  channel-major spatial merge and padding for odd image grids.
- Implement Ascend encoder graph configuration for the existing FIA
capture
and replay path. The inherited CUDA backend check rejects a `TORCH_SDPA`
  marker during initialization even though Ascend dispatches to FIA; the
  Ascend configuration avoids that incorrect rejection.
- Reuse existing budget selection, eager fallback, metadata preparation,
and
image-span postprocessing. No model-runner or global patch changes are
needed.

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

Yes. DeepSeek-V4.1 vision encoder ACL graphs can be enabled with:

```bash
--compilation-config '{"cudagraph_mm_encoder": true}'
```

The default eager path remains available. Inputs outside captured
budgets fall
back to eager execution. Image delimiter assembly remains outside the
graph.
The installed vLLM must provide the upstream encoder graph mixin.

[Performance] Remove redundant work from Kimi decode operators (#22346)

### What this PR does / why we need it?

This PR removes three sources of redundant work observed in Kimi K3.1
decode and incorporates the A3 Quantized Lightning Indexer (QLI) score
dtype fix from #22240.

#### Performance changes

1. **MoE: use a plain add for one tensor pair.** The shared MoE combine
adds the same shared and routed tensors directly, replacing the
one-element `torch._foreach_add` call. The measured reduction below is
for the profiled Kimi workload.
   - Implementation: `vllm_ascend/ops/fused_moe/fused_moe.py`.
2. **Indexer: skip the candidate fills and normalization on eligible A3
sharded DCP.** Pass each query row's rank-local visible KV length into
the pack stage. Plain packing, fused sort/pack, and separate sort
preparation mask padding and empty local prefixes before loading IDs or
scores. They still reject negative IDs and non-finite scores. The QLI
output initialization defaults to enabled and stays enabled when row
metadata is unavailable, including the existing A5 path. Candidate
exchange keeps its existing shape and layout. QLI v2 and v3 keep output
initialization enabled by default. The merge retains the upstream v3
candidate block length input and all four outputs.
- Row metadata and packing: `vllm_ascend/attention/indexer.py`,
`vllm_ascend/attention/context_parallel/sharded_indexer.py`,
`vllm_ascend/ops/triton/sharded_indexer.py`.
- QLI dispatch and optional initialization:
`vllm_ascend/device/device_op.py`,
`csrc/attention/quant_lightning_indexer_v2/quant_lightning_indexer_v2_torch_adpt.h`,
`csrc/torch_binding.cpp`, `csrc/torch_binding_meta.cpp`.
3. **Output projection: write into the supplied result slice.** SFA opts
into `AscendRowParallelLinear.try_forward_into()` for Kimi K3.1 decode.
SFA retains the existing NATIVE_INT8_SPARSE guard, which currently
limits this opt-in to A3. An eligible bias-free, unquantized row
projection without internal reduction uses `matmul(out=...)` to avoid
the explicit result assignment. Other cases keep the existing module
path.
- Linear dispatch: `vllm_ascend/ops/linear.py`. SFA call site:
`vllm_ascend/attention/sfa_v1.py`.

#### Bug fix from #22240

A3 QLI with `return_value=1` was returning FP32 scores. This change
restores BF16 output, matching A5. A3 native local candidates
(`return_value=2`) still return FP32 scores. Runtime allocation, Meta
inference and host dtype validation follow the same contract across both
the normal and split-and-merge kernel paths.

The candidate packer widens BF16 scores to FP32 for the existing
exchange format. The combined implementation uses the same pack-time
filtering for both changes, removing the standalone normalization kernel
once. Eligible A3 rows continue to use the no-Fill path with rank-local
visible lengths.

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

Yes. Direct A3 QLI callers using `return_value=1` now receive BF16 score
tensors instead of FP32. Callers that require an FP32 tensor can cast
the scores after the call. The cast preserves the BF16 values. The
supported model paths use the existing configuration.

### How was this patch tested?

#### Decode profiling before #22240 was incorporated

The supplied rank-0 1P1D traces are labeled 128K context and batch size
12. The baseline export contains 13 decode steps and the PR export
contains 11. Both traces show one index-mapping marker and 24 QLI calls
per step. Counts and summed device-kernel durations below are normalized
per decode step.

| Work measured | Baseline | PR build | Reduction per step |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| MoE shared and routed output add | 92 `ForeachAddList`, 1.698 ms | 92
replacement `Add`, 0.387 ms | 1.311 ms |
| A3 indexer candidate initialization | 48 `Fill`, 0.370 ms | 0 | 0.370
ms |
| A3 indexer candidate normalization | 24 kernels, 0.303 ms | 0 | 0.303
ms |
| A3 indexer candidate pack | 24 kernels, 0.771 ms | 24 kernels, 0.821
ms | −0.050 ms |
| **A3 indexer, total for the three rows above** | **1.443 ms** |
**0.821 ms** | **0.622 ms** |
| BF16 `o_proj` result copy | 24 `TensorMove`, 0.218 ms | 0 | 0.218 ms |

The MoE comparison matches the `[3, 7168]` output-add calls by shape and
their position in the surrounding MoE sequence, excluding five
same-shape `Add` calls already present in each baseline step. The
indexer `Fill` count is for candidate buffers with shape `[48, 1,
2048]`. Totals use unrounded durations.

For BF16 `o_proj`, each step has 24 matching `MatMulV2` calls after the
attention gate with `[48, 768]` activations and a `[48, 7168]` output.
In the baseline each is followed on the same stream by
`aclnnInplaceCopy` / `TensorMove` before ReduceScatter. The PR trace
goes directly to ReduceScatter. Matmul time per step is similar at 0.409
ms and 0.408 ms. The sum for matmul and result copy falls from 0.627 ms
to 0.408 ms.

The traces use different DCP reduction kernels. That change is outside
this patch. An end-to-end speedup remains unmeasured for this patch.
These captures come from an earlier PR build, before the merge with
upstream `main` and the integration of #22240.

#### Accuracy before #22240 was incorporated

Two GPQA runs with the PR applied scored **93.43%** and **93.94%**. A
GPQA baseline under the same settings and direct A3 output comparisons
are pending. Both scores describe model-level accuracy for the build
before #22240 was integrated.

#### Code verification

For `9bc8cbdd7`, the hardware profile, Linear, SFA forward, and SFA
context-parallel unit test files passed together (468 total) with the
vLLM commit listed below. The Linear test verifies direct dispatch to
the supplied buffer and checks fallback for bias, hooks, TP reduction,
and an invalid output shape.

All QSFA padding and DCP attention packing changes were dropped. The
related source and test files match the PR base, including the existing
post-QSFA padding handling and upstream DCP warmup. On the earlier
revision, 15 sharded-indexer unit tests passed in an isolated CPU run,

On the integrated revision (`d6cb13212`), Ruff lint and formatting,

was triggered for the integrated commit. A3 native tests and a fresh

The three affected kernels use dynamic, non-specialized row counts.
Packing geometry, strides, and sort tiles remain compile-time
parameters. The optional visible lengths add a None and an INT32 pointer
variant for each applicable path. Length values can change between

forwarding, and all three dispatch paths with mocked launches. Hardware

[Performance][A3][A5] Speed up packed DCP attention output combine (#21605)

### What this PR does / why we need it?

The shared DCP attention path merges partial outputs from separate K/V
shards, including an optional local result in split MLA attention. For
BF16 head scatter, this PR decodes each packed LSE once per output row
and reuses the rank weights across all features.

Runtime and warmup launch one Triton kernel. The device profile supplies
a compile-time row mode. A3 processes one row at a time because multirow
loads can lower to nested scalar loops. A5 processes eight rows per tile
to improve memory throughput. Each program owns a contiguous interval.
The same selection applies at every row count.

The optimized path accepts `D <= 512`, output-only combine and unit
local feature stride when a local output is present. Other supported
layouts and dtypes use the existing scalar path.

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

Packed DCP attention output combine is faster on the target A3 and A5
shapes. Callers use the existing API. The result includes the optional
local contribution once, masks outputs with nonfinite LSE and returns
zeros for all-invalid rows.

### How was this patch tested?

**Device-kernel performance.** The public wrapper ran on the same device
with the same inputs for each comparison. The table gives mean kernel
duration from two interleaved `msprof op` captures per side against
fixed main `6385299e`. Both shapes have 12 local heads, 512 features,
eight received ranks and one token-major local contribution.

| Device | Tokens | main (µs) | PR implementation (µs) | Speedup |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| A3 | 144 | 203.984 | 129.493 | 1.58× |
| A3 | 152 | 205.424 | 135.323 | 1.52× |
| A5 | 144 | 88.958 | 50.473 | 1.76× |
| A5 | 152 | 92.471 | 51.791 | 1.79× |

**Correctness and warmup.** At `6840da5c0`, the single-card DCP suite
passed 25/25 on each device. Four head-scatter cases use independently
encoded inputs and a CPU FP64 reduction, covering a single rank/feature,
received-only and local inputs, head-major strides, tails and invalid or
extreme LSE. The tests require finite output, at least 99% of elements
within `2e-5 + 0.004 * abs(reference)`, and maximum absolute error at
most 0.02.

Runtime and warmup select the same JIT function and mode. The device
contributes one mode per installation. Rank count, feature block size,
local contribution, pointer alignment and ordinary scalar specialization
can still produce variants. The two routing and warmup unit-test files
passed on the published head (41 tests). The A5 validation also passed
33 selected routing/warmup tests at `6840da5c0`.

Device tests and the timings above used `6840da5c0`. The published head
adds a kernel comment, removes a redundant terminal return and two
overlapping host test parameters, and condenses the documentation. The
single-card suite and kernel arithmetic are identical. Model-level
accuracy and throughput, distributed HCCL performance, and serving-time
compilation counts were not measured in this run.

pytest -q tests/ut/ops/test_dcp_a2a_combine.py tests/ut/model_executor/warmup/test_kernel_warmup.py

commits.message:
[Performance][MoE] Quantize W8A8 activations before PCP AllGather (#22230)

### What this PR does / why we need it?

The Ascend MoE ALLGATHER path gathers floating-point activations across
prefill context-parallel (PCP) ranks. Each rank then quantizes the
gathered rows during expert dispatch. For W8A8 INT8 and A5 W8A8 MXFP8
MoE, this change quantizes local padded rows before PCP AllGather. Each
rank gathers the activations together with their per-token INT8 scales
or per-block MXFP8 scales in matching row order. The existing Ascend
routing kernel consumes both tensors. Router logits retain their
existing gather, and DP still gathers before PCP.

The PCP optimization keeps floating-point inputs for LoRA, custom
routing functions, and layers that apply router weights to the input.
The existing EP sequence-parallel path continues to apply its own
quantization policy.

Upstream vLLM already uses the same ordering for eligible FP8 and NVFP4
kernels. This PR applies it to Ascend's W8A8 INT8 and MXFP8 paths, which
handle preparation and routing via `torch_npu`. [Upstream MoE
runner](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/0c4fe70662363193189f2212ecd9d55d39d5349e/vllm/model_executor/layers/fused_moe/runner/moe_runner.py)

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

Yes. Eligible W8A8 prefill workloads transfer fewer activation bytes and
avoid repeated quantization across PCP ranks. This applies automatically
with the existing configuration. The standalone and fused CANN
quantizers can differ by one INT8 quantization step.

### How was this patch tested?

- At `a18c97025`, the single two-rank PCP regression passed in 29.86 s
on two Ascend 950DT NPUs with CANN 9.3.0, torch-npu 2.10.0.post7 and
pinned vLLM `c410543d9fff`.
- The test gathers floating-point rows for the dispatch baseline and
compares them with quantization before the real HCCL gather. INT8 covers
local token counts (0, 5) and (4096, 4095), including zero padding and
8192 gathered rows. Routing indices and expert counts matched exactly,
and the routed INT8 activations matched within one quantization step.
- On A5 the same test also exercises both baseline MXFP8 dispatch paths
for (17, 9) and (0, 5) local tokens. The routed E4M3 payload and E8M0
block scales matched byte for byte. Both the default two-card selector
and the `ready-a5` suite select the shared test. The model accuracy and
throughput measurements below apply to the earlier INT8 candidate.

tests/e2e/pull_request/two_card/ops/test_pcp_quantized_routing.py

(DCP) enabled, an empty tail chunk could cause every rank to process an
entire prefill request. For example, a 225-token prefill on PCP8 fills
fifteen 15-token chunks and leaves the sixteenth empty. Reserving
capacity for 64 such requests inflates the target startup profile and
the prefill MC2/MegaMoE buffer.

In the Ascend MRV2 PCP manager, each rank keeps its full-width head
chunk. When fixed-width slicing would leave an empty tail, the manager
distributes the remaining tokens across the tails if all ranks can
receive one. A 225-token prefill then gives each rank 28 or 29 tokens.
Every rank has two chunks with a longest chunk of 15, so the sparse
Indexer derives the same planning charge of 30 on every rank. Dispatch,
KV write deduplication and hidden-state restoration use this layout
through the existing PCP manager interfaces.

For PCP size `P > 1`, the largest prefill that still needs replication
is `3P - 1`: at that length the heads consume `2P` tokens and only `P -
1` tail tokens remain. The startup budget uses that bound together with
speculative verification length, rounding and the existing prefill graph
floor. This follows up on #21985 and #22656.

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

Yes. Short prefills with PCP and DCP can do less replicated work, and
the local prefill MC2/MegaMoE reservation can shrink. With eager
execution, PCP8/DCP8, TP1, 64 sequences, 16,384 batched tokens and three
DSpark speculative tokens, the target and prefill MC2 budget changes
from **14,776 to 3,464 rows**. DSpark retains its 16,384-row global
context budget. The change applies to the shared Ascend MRV2 path and
requires no new configuration.

At a global `--max-num-batched-tokens` of 24,576, the same eager
configuration reduces the prefill MegaMoE row limit from **15,800 to

communication and workspace reservation per rank** (1.29 GiB
communication and 6.40 GiB workspace, rounded independently). This
leaves room for transient allocations while serving larger batches with

commits.message:
[BugFix] Fix prefill crash for KV-sharing consumer layers (Gemma-4) (#23008)

## What this PR does / why we need it?
Fixes #21972
Gemma-4 uses YOCO-style KV sharing: layers marked `is_kv_shared_layer`
have no `k_proj`/`v_proj` and call attention as `attn(q, None, None)`.
They produce no K/V of their own and can only read the KV cache written
by their producer layer.

The Ascend `PrefillNoCache` path is a dense-KV bypass: `_get_fia_params`
returns `key`/`value` unchanged with `block_table=None`, and the caller
then trims the dense K/V via `key = key[:num_tokens]`. For a consumer
layer `key` is `None`, so any model with KV sharing (currently Gemma-4
and the Gemma-4 MTP drafter) crashes during prefill with:

```
TypeError: 'NoneType' object is not subscriptable
```

at `forward_fused_infer_attention` -> `key = key[:num_tokens]`.

This PR makes the backend recognize a KV-sharing consumer (`key is
None`): `_get_fia_params` requires the paged cache view instead of the
dense bypass, the dense K/V trimming is skipped, and
`is_prefill_no_cache` is passed as `False` to `DeviceOperator` so the
consumer is handled as paged KV on the large-head prefill path. The C8
path also initializes the producer cache handle, because the consumer
layer skips `_reshape_and_cache`.

## Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

Yes. Gemma-4 (including the MTP drafter) previously failed during
prefill on Ascend NPU; it now runs.

## How was this patch tested?

Hardware: A3 (single die, `ASCEND_RT_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0`),
`enforce_eager=True`, `gemma-4-E4B-it` with `gemma-4-E4B-it-assistant`.
Baseline (no speculative decoding) and MTP (`method=mtp`,
`num_speculative_tokens=2`) both complete and shut down cleanly.
`llm.chat` on three prompts returns identical, correct results for both
runs: `Paris` / `391` / `Jupiter` (3/3 match). Before the fix, the same
script deterministically raised the `TypeError` above in
`forward_fused_infer_attention`.

Existing e2e coverage does not reach this path: the 31B target has
`num_kv_shared_layers=0`, and the 31B drafter's prefill state is
rewritten to `PrefillCacheHit` by the Gemma-4 speculator, so
`test_gemma4_mtp_spec_decode_model_runner_v2` would not catch a
regression here. The only configuration that runs a consumer layer in
`PrefillNoCache` is the E4B target (18/42 shared layers), which is what
the manual test above uses. A new unit test
(`test_kv_sharing_consumer_prefill_reads_producer_cache`) covers this
combination directly: a consumer layer in `PrefillNoCache` must return
the producer cache view, a non-`None` block table, and `seq_lens_list`
as the KV lengths.

Graph mode: with `cudagraph_mode=FULL_DECODE_ONLY` the baseline run
completes and shuts down cleanly. The MTP run fails only during FULL
graph capture with `aclnnFusedInferAttentionScoreV3 ... 561002` (`When D
is 512, inputlayout TND q_rope and k_rope should not be null`), raised
from `_npu_fused_infer_attention_score_get_max_workspace` while
capturing the draft model. This is the pre-existing Gemma-4 512-dim TND
limitation tracked in #19559, not caused by this change: the FIA call
path never passes `q_rope`/`k_rope` regardless of KV sharing. With
`cudagraph_mode=PIECEWISE`, MTP completes and returns correct answers
(`The capital of France is Paris`, `The largest planet in the solar
system is Jupiter`; the arithmetic prompt was cut off by `max_tokens=16`
before producing the number).

Unit tests: `pytest tests/ut/attention/test_attention_v1.py -k
kv_sharing` -> 3 passed, 45 deselected. AI assistance was used to
prepare this change; the diff and the test runs above were reviewed
manually.

[Feature][KV Pool] Support DeepSeek-V4 layerwise KV offload (#22024)

### What this PR does / why we need it?

Enable DeepSeek-V4 Flash and Pro to reuse shared HBM buffers on the
Prefill side with the layerwise KV offload framework from #21256.
Layerwise reuse lowers the HBM footprint per global KV block so the same
Prefill KV budget can hold more blocks.

Reuse covers the target model's C4 and C128 compressed history, indexer
history, sliding-window KV, and compressor states. The save path keeps
the public prefix pages selected by the coordinator and adds the live
window needed for the next chunk. Chunk continuation restores the live
window. SWA-only layers use the registered SWA cache name for Mooncake
Push. Shared buffers wait for Store saves and relevant P-to-D sends
before reuse, using the transfer dependency introduced in #21891.

### User-visible changes

Shared buffers require the top-level role to be `kv_producer`. Prefill
combines `AscendStoreConnector` and `MooncakePushConnector` through
`MultiConnector`. The P/D proxy caps Prefill requests at one generated
token. Decode uses resident HBM caches and the MTP draft cache stays
resident. Combining shared-buffer reuse with DSpark is deferred.

Set these options on the Prefill AscendStore child connector. This
example keeps layers 0 and 1 resident. Set the independent layer list to
`[]` to allow the first two SWA layers to participate in reuse. Omit
`layerwise_num_shared_buffers` for regular layerwise pooling.

```json
{
  "backend": "memcache",
  "use_layerwise": true,
  "layerwise_num_shared_buffers": 3,
  "layerwise_prefetch_layers": 4,
  "layerwise_independent_layers": [0, 1]
}
```

### How was this patch tested?

#### CPU unit test coverage

- Flash and Pro cache planning, producer-only role validation, and MTP
draft-cache residency.
- SWA checkpoint saves and chunk-continuation loads, private GVA
snapshot fallback, and PCP publication ordering.
- SWA-only Mooncake Push dispatch, connector dependencies, and Qwen4Exp
layerwise cache reuse regression coverage.

#### Single-host 950PR P/D functional test

The archived run used DeepSeek-V4 Flash with P TP4 and D TP4,
PP=DP=PCP=DCP=1, EP, Model Runner V2, PIECEWISE graphs, FP8 target and
indexer KV, and one MTP draft token. Prefill used Memcache with three
shared buffers, prefetch depth 2, and no independent layers. Decode used
resident HBM. Local HBM prefix caching was disabled on both sides. The
Prefill chunk was 1,024 tokens, the maximum model length was 4,096, and
GPU memory utilization was 0.86. The tested snapshot was `a64a61c6b`
with #21262 and its integration changes applied.

| 3/3 | 2,067 | 64 | 6,198 | 104 proposed, 91 accepted, 13 rejected |

The first two SWA layers participated in reuse. Decode set the KV load

#### Two-host 950DT P/D performance

The archived Flash benchmark used `09adb5d33` with #21262 and the
integration changes used at the time. Prefill and Decode each ran on one
A5 950DT host at TP8 with PP=DP=PCP=DCP=1. Both used EP, Model Runner

[Performance][KV Transfer] Optimize Mooncake V2 addresses and SWA metadata (#22661)

### What this PR does / why we need it?

Long-context Mooncake V2 transfers spend CPU time building per-block
Python objects and repeating address arithmetic across layers. Pull
metadata also carries SWA block IDs outside the retained window.

This PR:

- Represents block transfer ranges as NumPy arrays and builds singleton
or contiguous ranges only when the layout needs them. Reuses
request-scoped byte offsets and length lists across matching pull
layouts within a spec/remote bucket, with scalar arithmetic for a single
range.
- Vectorizes Push descriptor arithmetic and reuses request-ordered block
arrays across cache components.
- Trims Pull SWA metadata to the retained suffix after speculative-block
trimming. Retention includes `extra_retained_tokens`, the largest
combined window in a uniform group, and an unaligned boundary page. The
receiver recovers the suffix's logical start before intersecting it with
the consumer's unhashed blocks, preserving prefix-hit and block-scale
mapping.

NumPy/address caching and SWA trimming are separate commits. READ/WRITE
still receive Python integer lists; no Mooncake array API or dependency
upgrade is required. Existing byte-contiguity rules, descriptor order,
partial-head offsets, independent P/D strides, and completion/failure
handling are preserved. Mamba keeps its separate address path.

Inspired by the vectorized descriptor approach in
vllm-project/vllm#62478. This PR is independent of #20903 (per-request
submission and pool configuration).

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

No.

### How was this patch tested?

**CPU correctness on ARM in the A3 runtime (before rebase):**

- 445 pull-worker and push-sending tests passed for the NumPy/cache
commit.
- 603 pull-worker, scheduler, SWA-handoff and virtual-pull tests passed
for the final SWA commit, including three retention cases covering extra
retained tokens across page boundaries and different retention windows
within a group.
- Address coverage includes empty/singleton and fragmented inputs,
padded and partial-head layouts, independent strides, high addresses,
descriptor ordering, and reuse of computed address components.
- Tests imported the candidate Mooncake Python package through an
isolated source overlay. These CPU tests do not exercise native
transport or prove NPU numerical accuracy.

**Full P/D serving on ARM/Ascend:**

Both runs used the pre-rebase `631d988` source, with imported module
paths and hashes checked. Warmup was excluded from the reported
benchmark windows. Baselines below are historical runs using the
corresponding workload/configuration, not alternating concurrent A/B
experiments.

| A5: 8 x Ascend 950DT, DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731 | Earlier V2 with SWA
trimming | Hybrid | This PR |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Mean TTFT (s) | 45.000 | 40.215 | 39.390 |
| P99 TTFT (s) | 91.766 | 97.990 | 95.014 |
| Mean TPOT (ms) | 17.9 | 16.3 | 15.9 |
| Mean ITL (ms) | 111.2 | 102.8 | 103.4 |
| Output throughput (token/s) | 11312.957 | 12538.458 | 12785.476 |

A5 configuration: P/D each DP4/TP1/PCP1/EP4; KV/indexer FP8; DSpark5
with actual acceptance; 16 proxy workers; 3,200 requests at concurrency
800, each with 131,155 input tokens and 1,024 output tokens. P used
eager execution; D used async scheduling and FULL_DECODE_ONLY, with
prefix caching disabled. vLLM
`62d4bc3c7e33b1b6c906e233e6af2d3506c482ca`, Ascend image base
`7dcdb690caf879a17ab07382880d5773f5202e20`, torch 2.10.0+cpu and
torch_npu 2.10.0.post7. All 3,200 requests completed successfully. Mean
TTFT was 12.47% lower and throughput 13.02% higher than the earlier V2
baseline. Relative to Hybrid, TTFT was 2.05% lower and throughput 1.97%
higher; a single historical comparison does not establish a stable 2%
advantage. P99 TTFT was higher than the earlier V2 baseline, and mean
ITL slightly higher than Hybrid.

| A3: DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731-w8a8 | Hybrid | This PR |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Mean TTFT (s) | 3.204 | 3.327 |
| P99 TTFT (s) | 9.488 | 9.701 |
| Mean TPOT (ms) | 33.323 | 33.439 |
| Output throughput (token/s) | 10575.552 | 10537.377 |

A3 configuration: P/D each DP8/TP1/EP8; 16 proxy workers; 1,600 requests
at concurrency 400, 65,538 input tokens and 1,000 output tokens, with
65,536-token D prefix hits. DSpark used synthetic acceptance length 4,
so this is not an actual-acceptance accuracy test. All 1,600 requests
completed successfully without request retries. Throughput was within
0.36% of historical Hybrid; mean TTFT remained 3.86% higher.

These serving runs validate performance and request completion for the
stated cases, not independent numerical parity or every layout/topology.
End-to-end differences cannot be attributed entirely to address
construction. Push performance and NPU numerical parity remain
unmeasured; required CI remains pending.

**Local repository checks on the submitted commit:** Ruff check/format,
spelling, C++ formatting, Markdown, PNG,
filename/package/import/context-manager hooks, and `git diff --check`
passed. Actionlint environment installation stalled on Windows;
actionlint, gitleaks and shellcheck remain for CI. The
logger/long-function/symbolic-meta hook launchers encountered Windows
`/bin/bash` or `python3` path issues. Equivalent native-Python logger
scanning, the long-function checker applied to added PR lines, and the
native-Python symbolic-meta check passed separately.

**Rebase validation (2026-11-26):** Rebased onto upstream
`5e4e3a22f1a95bcd6d61d0389bb390067899076a`; the rebase produced
`f1d22fd5b`. The only textual conflict was the pull-worker utility
import: preserve upstream's `worker_rank_to_dcp_rank` while removing the
obsolete grouping import. Upstream's version-dependent DCP routing fix
is retained in both Pull and Push. AST comparisons confirm the
address-optimization and SWA methods are unchanged. Sixty
source-isolated CPU checks passed for the rank helper and Pull grouping
across both ordering modes and TP/PCP/DCP combinations. Supported
repository hooks and `git diff --check` passed. NPU
serving/accuracy/performance were not rerun after rebase; the ARM and
serving results above belong to the pre-rebase revision.

**Test simplification (`7d4c0428c`):** Consolidated overlapping Pull
cache tests into the existing cross-layer range-reuse test and reduced
the SWA Cartesian matrix to six explicit boundary cases, including extra
retention across a page boundary. This removes 76 test lines and eight
cases while retaining request/call isolation, independent strides,
different transfer lengths, and suffix/prefix-hit coverage. The two
release-note YAML fragments were removed; production code is unchanged.
After rebase and simplification, 610 tests passed on the ARM A5 runtime
across `test_pull_worker.py`, `test_pull_scheduler.py`,
`test_push_sending.py`, `test_swa_handoff.py`, and
`test_virtual_pull.py`, using an isolated source overlay with hashes
checked. Supported repository hooks and `git diff --check` passed. No
model services or NPU workload were started.

AI assistance was used for implementation and validation.

### Checklist

- [x] Address-generation and retained-window regression tests
- [x] ARM CPU runtime tests
- [x] A3 and A5 full P/D serving performance measurements
- [ ] Independent NPU numerical parity
- [ ] Required CI checks

[Feature][Model] Adopt fused MsaIndexScore TopK with forced-block support (#23122)

### What this PR does / why we need it?

MiniMax-M3's fused index-score Top-K
(`cann_ops_transformer.msa_index_score`
with `return_choice`) was gated behind a new hardware capability,
`HardwareCapability.MINIMAX_M3_INDEX_SCORE_TOPK_FUSION`, and therefore
enabled
on A5 only. A2, A3 and A5 all run the same CANN operator, and A2/A3
behave
identically, so this capability gate carried no real information. It
only made
A2/A3 run a separate score pass, Top-K and sort on every index-score
step.

This PR removes the hardware gate. The fused path is now decided solely
by
whether the installed CANN package provides the fused output:

- `vllm_ascend/models/minimax_m3/ops/msa_m3_npu.py`:
  `_can_use_index_score_topk_fusion()` no longer calls

`get_current_hardware_profile().supports(MINIMAX_M3_INDEX_SCORE_TOPK_FUSION)`.
The two real constraints stay: `0 < topk <= 128` with `topk % 8 == 0`
(the
operator's non-aligned write-back returns uninitialised memory for
multi-token
  requests), and the `_index_score_has_return_choice()` signature probe.
  Docstrings are updated to match.
- `vllm_ascend/device/hardware_profile.py`: removes the
`HardwareCapability.MINIMAX_M3_INDEX_SCORE_TOPK_FUSION` enum member with
its
comment, and its registration in the A5 profile. No references remain
anywhere
  in the tree.

Behavior:
- A3 (and A2, when the same CANN package is installed): prefill and
sorted
decode with an aligned `topk` now take the fused path and skip the
separate
  `_minimax_m3_index_score` plus `_minimax_m3_index_prefill_topk` /
  `index_decode_topk_fused` calls.
- A5: unchanged.
- A CANN package without `return_choice`: still falls back to the
separate path.
- An unaligned `topk`: still falls back to the separate path.

Fixes # (add the related issue if one exists)

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

No. No configuration key, environment variable, API or default switch is
added
or changed. `MINIMAX_M3_INDEX_SCORE_TOPK_FUSION` is an internal
`HardwareCapability` enum member and was never exposed to users. The
only
observable difference is index-score path performance for MiniMax-M3 on
A2/A3;
the computed indices are unchanged.

### How was this patch tested?

Unit tests, run on this revision (`main` + this PR) in the `pxt_test_v2`
container:

```bash
pytest tests/ut/device/test_hardware_profile.py tests/ut/models/minimax_m3/test_msa_m3.py -q
# 626 passed
```

The cases touched by this PR:

```bash
pytest tests/ut/device/test_hardware_profile.py tests/ut/models/minimax_m3/test_msa_m3.py \
  -q -k "fusion or fused or a2_a3 or index_score"
# 44 passed, 582 deselected

pytest "tests/ut/models/minimax_m3/test_msa_m3.py::test_topk_fusion_is_enabled_on_a2_a3_and_a5" \
       "tests/ut/models/minimax_m3/test_msa_m3.py::test_ascendc_index_prefill_uses_fused_topk_on_a2_a3" -v
# test_topk_fusion_is_enabled_on_a2_a3_and_a5             PASSED
# test_ascendc_index_prefill_uses_fused_topk_on_a2_a3[a2] PASSED
# test_ascendc_index_prefill_uses_fused_topk_on_a2_a3[a3] PASSED
```

Test changes:
- `test_topk_fusion_is_enabled_on_a5_only` becomes
`test_topk_fusion_is_enabled_on_a2_a3_and_a5`: A5, A3 and A2 all assert
  `True`, where A3 and A2 previously asserted `False`.
- New parameterized fixture `fused_index_ops_a2_a3` (`a2` / `a3`) and
new
`test_ascendc_index_prefill_uses_fused_topk_on_a2_a3`, which asserts
that an
aligned `topk` on A2/A3 calls `msa_index_score(return_choice=1, topk=16,
local_blocks=1)` directly and that neither the separate score path nor
the
  separate Top-K path is called.

cover `_index_score_has_return_choice` returning `False`, which is the

`MINIMAX_M3_INDEX_SCORE_TOPK_FUSION` from the expected A5 capability

[BugFix][Upstream] Tolerate a missing backend attribute in GroupCoordinator destroy (#22192)

### What this PR does / why we need it?

`GroupCoordinatorPatch.destroy()` in
`vllm_ascend/patch/worker/patch_distributed.py`
reads `self.backend` to decide whether the device process group is owned
by the
HCCL registry (backend `hccl`) or has to be destroyed directly:

```python
device_group = getattr(self, "device_group", None)
if device_group is not None and self.backend != "hccl":
    torch.distributed.destroy_process_group(device_group)
```

`backend` is only assigned in `GroupCoordinatorPatch.__init__`. The
upstream
vLLM test
`tests/distributed/test_flashinfer_pcie_ipc_all_reduce.py::test_group_destroy_releases_communicator_before_process_groups`
builds a coordinator with `GroupCoordinator.__new__(GroupCoordinator)`,
so
`backend` is never set. With the vllm-ascend patch installed, the call
fails
before the test can assert the destroy order:

```
AttributeError: 'GroupCoordinatorPatch' object has no attribute 'backend'
vllm_ascend/patch/worker/patch_distributed.py:227: in destroy
```

This is the failure reported in #21966 (weekly `upstream-test` shard).

This PR reads the backend with `getattr` and treats a missing value as
"not hccl", so the device group is destroyed directly. That matches the
upstream `GroupCoordinator.destroy()`, which always destroys the device
group,
and it keeps the NPU production path unchanged: the Ascend backend is
always
`hccl`, so the device group stays owned by the registry and is released
by
`_release_hccl_resources()` as before.

Fixes #21966

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

No behaviour change for a running engine: the Ascend backend is always
`hccl`,
so the production destroy path is bit-for-bit the same. The change only
removes
the `AttributeError` on a destroy path that previously crashed, which
also fixes
the upstream vLLM test suite when the vllm-ascend patch is installed. A
release
note fragment is included (`release_notes/fragments/22192.yaml`).

### How was this patch tested?

#### CPU unit test (new)

- Regression test:

`tests/ut/patch/worker/patch_common/test_patch_distributed.py::test_destroy_without_backend_attribute_releases_groups_in_order`
It builds a `GroupCoordinatorPatch` through `__new__` (so `backend` is
never
assigned), attaches a fake device communicator plus a device and a CPU
process
group, and asserts that `destroy()` releases the communicator before the
two
process groups - the same order the upstream test requires. Without this
  change the test fails with
`AttributeError: 'GroupCoordinatorPatch' object has no attribute
'backend'`
  at `vllm_ascend/patch/worker/patch_distributed.py:227`.
- Local CPU run of the whole module: **18 passed**
(`python -m pytest
tests/ut/patch/worker/patch_common/test_patch_distributed.py -q`).

#### Upstream vLLM test (the one #21966 is about)

The upstream test was run directly with the vllm-ascend patch applied
(`adapt_patch()`), against vLLM
`vllm@c410543d9ffff03f5f6c4a8c0ae1d3ad082c4a15`:

| | result |
|---|---|
| without this fix | **FAILED** - `AttributeError:
'GroupCoordinatorPatch' object has no attribute 'backend'` at
`patch_distributed.py:227` |
| with this fix | **PASSED** |

#### Real-NPU validation (new)

`tests/manual/test_group_coordinator_destroy_npu.py` validates on real
Ascend
hardware that the production path really is unchanged, instead of only
asserting it. It was run on **2 x Ascend 910B3** (torch_npu
2.10.0.post4,
CANN 9.1.0, vLLM v0.33.0):

```
torchrun --nproc_per_node=2 tests/manual/test_group_coordinator_destroy_npu.py
```

The script creates a **real** HCCL process group, runs a collective over
it,
and checks that `destroy()` releases the device group **exactly once
through the
HCCL registry** while the gloo cpu group is destroyed directly, that the
registry holds no dangling entry afterwards, and that a fresh HCCL group
can
still be created and used on the same devices afterwards.

Differential result on the same hardware:

| check | pre-fix | with this fix |
|---|---|---|
| coordinator backend is `hccl` on Ascend | PASS | PASS |
| real HCCL device group was created | PASS | PASS |
| `all_reduce` over the real HCCL group works (got 2.0) | PASS | PASS |
| coordinator acquired an HCCL registry key | PASS | PASS |
| hccl device group destroyed exactly once (by the registry) | PASS |
PASS |
| `destroy()` destroyed exactly the device group and the cpu group |
PASS | PASS |
| gloo cpu group destroyed directly | PASS | PASS |
| `device_group` / `cpu_group` attributes deleted | PASS | PASS |
| coordinator holds no HCCL registry key after `destroy()` | PASS | PASS
|
| a fresh HCCL group can be created after `destroy()` | PASS | PASS |
| `all_reduce` works on the fresh group | PASS | PASS |
| orphan coordinator (no `backend` attribute) is destroyable |
**AttributeError** | PASS |
| orphan coordinator destroyed its device group directly | (not reached)
| PASS |
| script exit code | 1 | **0** |

So every NPU-path check behaves identically before and after the change,
and
the only difference is the previously crashing case.

The device group is destroyed exactly once in both cases because the
HCCL
registry's `release()` itself calls
`torch.distributed.destroy_process_group`.
The check therefore counts the destroy calls rather than just asserting
the
group was not destroyed directly, which would not have distinguished the
two
code paths.

#### Other checks

- `ruff check` and `ruff format --check` on the changed files: passed.
- Repository pre-commit hooks (`check_python_src_init`,
`check_forbidden_imports`,
`check_boolean_context_manager`, `check_long_functions`,
`check_logger`): passed.
- `codespell` on the changed files: passed.

### Checklist

#### Testing

- [x] **Boundary / edge-case coverage**: the regression test covers a
coordinator that never went through `__init__`, i.e. the only case in
which
  `backend` is missing. The existing tests keep covering the `hccl` and
  non-`hccl` backends.
- [x] **Regression test**:
`test_destroy_without_backend_attribute_releases_groups_in_order` fails
  without this fix.
- [x] **Error / failure path coverage**: the test drives the `destroy()`
path
  that previously raised `AttributeError`.
- [x] **Meaningful & reliable tests**: the test asserts the real destroy
order
(communicator before the process groups it depends on), not internal
state.
The NPU script additionally exercises a real HCCL group with a
collective,
  not a mock.
- [x] **Performance impact**: the change only replaces an attribute
lookup with
a `getattr` on the group teardown path, which runs once per process
group at
  shutdown.

[Feature][A3] Integrate K3.1 DSpark MLA with device-side tiling (#23221)

### What this PR does / why we need it?

Integrate the community A3 MLA provider for eligible Kimi K3.1 DSpark
draft decode. The draft prepares a schedule from device lengths with
`get_scheduler_metadata` and passes it to `flash_attn_with_kvcache`. If
the provider or a required entry point is unavailable, the existing
backend handles decode.

A3 FULL proposal skips the metadata result that would be discarded. The
graph manager builds the metadata through the upstream uniform helper
and refreshes the captured schedules once per replay. In split DCP this
refresh prepares one history schedule and one current-token schedule.
Eager and piecewise proposals still build metadata in the normal entry
point.

The connector capability check recognizes a single built-in MooncakeV2
child and applies the existing layerwise restriction. Cache allocation,
writes and backend selection share the final layout decision, including
the validated deployment restrictions for a wrapper.

### Does this PR introduce any user-facing change?

Supported A3 DSpark draft decode can use the [native
provider](https://github.com/MinghuasLab/flash-attention-npu) without a
new configuration option. The provider-only commit `d20db138e` retains
the corrected token-count copy and next-step event wait for comparison.
The separately reviewable commit `48b57b0df` skips both on eligible A3
Kimi configurations through the existing model-state hooks. At KV
initialization Kimi checks the active consumers. The scheduler keeps its
host upper bound while execution uses corrected device lengths.

This branch supports eligible single-rank decode. Multi-rank split
execution requires the DCP changes in #23220. Without split support it
keeps the existing backend.

### How was this patch tested?

- At `48b57b0df`, 148 CPU attention tests passed and 7 skipped. Combined
with #23220 at `4ff444bad`, the attention and DCP output-mask suites had
157 passes and 17 skips.
- An additional 16 isolated CPU cases passed on both trees. These
exercised the production Kimi hooks and runner copy/update methods with
PyTorch CPU tensors and stand-ins for unavailable runtime dependencies
and stream events. They covered rejection and reordered requests, DCP
sizes 1 and 8, native RecoverSSM on/off, A3 native vs FIA,
reinitialization, unsupported consumers and the existing A5 decision.
- A RecoverSSM page-boundary regression test is included for the full
vLLM environment and was not run locally. This revision has no new NPU
profiling or serving measurement.

[Feature][Sleep Mode] Discard parameter-only weights at level 2 (#22629)

### What this PR does / why we need it?

This is the P2 follow-up to the merged P1 integration (#22822) of
https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-ascend/issues/22572. P1 moved
Ascend sleep/wake onto `SleepModeBackend`; this PR implements the
upstream
discardable level-2 contract so level 2 no longer keeps Python copies of
the
whole model.

Changes:

- Discard only weights allocations whose blocks are exclusively
rewritten
parameters or inactive. Mixed and non-parameter allocations are backed
up
  to host and restored on wake-up.
- Keep `sleep_preserve_parameter_names` semantics by excluding preserved
  parameter storages from the discardable set.
- Remove the Python level-2 parameter/buffer snapshots; the allocator's
CPU
  backups now provide the restore path.
- Align `CaMemAllocator.sleep`, `discard`, `wake_up`, and
`use_memory_pool`
  with the upstream structure, using NPU CPU backup, memcpy, and unmap
  primitives, including the CPU backup release hook.
- Remove Ascend's local `_get_sleep_parameters()` / `get_draft_model()`
  overrides and inherit the upstream implementations. 

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

Yes, the sleep-mode memory policy changes, but the public API/CLI is
unchanged.

- **Level 2:**
- Parameter-only weights allocations are discarded without a CPU backup
and
    restored by the caller's weight reload.
- Mixed and non-parameter weights-pool allocations are backed up to CPU
and
restored on wake-up instead of being discarded with the whole weights
pool.
- `sleep_preserve_parameter_names` continues to retain selected
parameters.
- Draft parameters are now included as `draft.*`, matching upstream.
Callers
should preserve them with `sleep_preserve_parameter_names=["draft.*"]`
or
    restore them through the separate draft weight-update path.

- **Level 1:**
- Weights and `runtime` / `cudagraph` allocations are backed up, while
KV
    cache and other non-offloaded tags are discarded.
- This matches upstream `CuMemBackend.suspend()`. Ascend currently tags
only
`weights` and `kv_cache`, so there is no observable level-1 change in
    current models; the additional tags are for future runtime/cudagraph
    allocations.

- `--enable-sleep-mode` and the sleep/wake API are unchanged.

A release note is added in `release_notes/fragments/22629.yaml`.

### Compatibility and limitations

- **torch_npu 2.10:** `MemPool.snapshot()` is unavailable, so the
allocator
uses `torch.npu.memory_snapshot()` and filters to live weights
allocations.
  Per-pool snapshots can replace this fallback once torch_npu 2.13 is
  supported.
- Because per-pool snapshots are unavailable on the current pin,
  `CaMemAllocator._trim` and `CaMemAllocator.cudagraph_pool` raise
  `NotImplementedError`; `use_memory_pool` does not call `_trim`.

[Feature][HiSparse] Mooncake MemFabric Pull into shared Offload Host (#22109)

## What changes

Extend #20926 with direct P/D Pull from ordinary Prefill KV into
HiSparse on Decode. Set `transfer_backend=memfabric` in
`MooncakeConnectorV2` to select the native MemFabric TransferEngine.
Decode pulls MLA main KV directly into its MemFabric Offload Host Source
and Indexer KV into each rank's NPU.

- In shared mode, Decode TP rank 0 contributes the shared Host backing,
imports main KV and writes new main KV back. Other ranks attach to the
backing. Each rank keeps its own Indexer, Resident and Hot buffers.
- The transfer engine registers Prefill source regions and Decode
destinations. On Decode, it registers the entire Host allocation once,
including padding.
- URMA requests reuse a selected Prefill KV replica to reduce concurrent
session setup. P and D use matching TP. Decode requires PCP=1 and
Prefill requires DCP=1. Prefill PCP>1 is covered by targeted address
tests and still needs end-to-end NPU validation.

## Core pairing and Ascend Worker

Build with unmodified [vLLM Core
`c410543d9ffff03f5f6c4a8c0ae1d3ad082c4a15`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/commit/c410543d9ffff03f5f6c4a8c0ae1d3ad082c4a15),
pinned in `.github/vllm-main-verified.commit`.

- `AscendHiSparseConnectorWorker` extends the upstream HiSparse worker
with Ascend DMA setup, recycled-block invalidation, H→D DMA for batched
Host-to-Resident restore, and TP synchronization for rank-0 Host
writeback.
- `AscendHiSparseOffloadManager` takes the engine configuration from the
existing `HiSparseHostPool` instance and owns the physical Host
allocation and sharing.
- The Decode `MultiConnector` combination can overlap Target Host
writeback with MTP drafting and waits for the Host copy before reporting
readiness.

## A5 startup example

On each node, set `MODEL_PATH` to the local GLM-5.2 W4A8C8 model
directory and `VLLM_HOST_IP` to the node's own reachable address. The
example uses TP8 and PCP=1 on both sides. Send inference requests
through a P/D proxy.

```bash
# Run on both nodes in the matching vLLM Ascend environment.
export MODEL_PATH=/path/to/GLM-5.2-W4A8C8
export VLLM_HOST_IP='REPLACE_WITH_LOCAL_NODE_IP'
export VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=1
export ASCEND_RT_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0,1,2,3,4,5,6,7
COMMON_ARGS=(
  --served-model-name glm52-w4a8c8 --host "$VLLM_HOST_IP"
  --tensor-parallel-size 8 --dtype bfloat16 --quantization ascend
  --kv-cache-dtype fp8 --block-size 128 --max-model-len 139264
  --max-num-batched-tokens 1024 --max-num-seqs 8 --gpu-memory-utilization 0.8
  --reasoning-parser glm47
)
```

**Prefill (ordinary KV, eager)**

```bash
vllm serve "$MODEL_PATH" "${COMMON_ARGS[@]}" --port 18100 \
  --enforce-eager --enable-prefix-caching \
  --attention-config '{"indexer_kv_dtype":"fp8"}' \
  --kv-transfer-config '{
    "kv_connector":"MooncakeConnectorV2", "kv_role":"kv_producer", "kv_port":31300,
    "kv_connector_extra_config":{"transfer_backend":"memfabric","memfabric_transfer_protocol":"device_urma"}
  }'
```

**Decode (HiSparse, `FULL_DECODE_ONLY`)**

```bash
vllm serve "$MODEL_PATH" "${COMMON_ARGS[@]}" --port 18101 \
  --no-enable-prefix-caching \
  --compilation-config '{"cudagraph_mode":"FULL_DECODE_ONLY","cudagraph_capture_sizes":[1,2,4,8]}' \
  --attention-config '{"indexer_kv_dtype":"fp8","hisparse_config":{"eager_host_mirror":true}}' \
  --kv-transfer-config '{
    "kv_connector":"MultiConnector", "kv_role":"kv_consumer", "kv_port":31400,
    "kv_connector_extra_config":{"connectors":[
      {"kv_connector":"HiSparseConnector","kv_role":"kv_consumer",
        "kv_connector_extra_config":{"host_pool_gib":32.0}},
      {"kv_connector":"MooncakeConnectorV2","kv_role":"kv_consumer","kv_port":31400,
        "kv_connector_extra_config":{"transfer_backend":"memfabric","memfabric_transfer_protocol":"device_urma"}}
    ]}
  }'
```

Keep `HiSparseConnector` first in the Decode `MultiConnector` list. To
reproduce the MTP functional check, add `--speculative-config
'{"method":"mtp","num_speculative_tokens":1}'` to both commands.

## Full-model A5 validation

Validated at `820de494de` with GLM-5.2 W4A8C8 and TP8 per node. Prefill
ran in eager mode with HiSparse disabled. Decode used HiSparse with
`FULL_DECODE_ONLY`. Transfer used native MemFabric `1.5.0.dev20261115`
with `transfer_backend=memfabric` and
`memfabric_transfer_protocol=device_urma`.

- **GPQA Diamond** — 178/198 correct (89.90%). All 198 requests
returned. Six responses hit the 131,072-token limit. No MemFabric
connection failures were observed during the concurrency-8 resume.
- **Prefill-only** — 65,536 input tokens, one output token, zero
prefix-cache hits. All 24 requests passed at concurrency 1. Mean/P90
TTFT was 16.758/16.773 s. Input throughput was 3,908.42 tokens/s.
- **Decode-only** — 65,536 prefix tokens cached per request, one
additional token computed for initial logits, and 1,024 output tokens.
All 24 requests passed at concurrency 1. Mean/P90 TTFT was 143.83/151.32
ms, mean TPOT was 24.40 ms, and output throughput was 40.79 tokens/s.
- **P/D + HiSparse + MTP** — All eight requests with 301- or 2,100-token
inputs matched the non-MTP continuations. Decode confirmed KV Pull,
target and draft graph replay, and overlap of rank-0 Host writeback with
drafting. MTP accepted 24 of 45 proposed tokens. High-concurrency MTP
performance remains untested.

## Earlier reduced-model measurements

An earlier A5 eager run with 10-layer GLM-5.3 MXFP8 and P/D TP2 matched
local Decode on eight-token continuations for 5, 301, 2,049, 4,097 and
8,193 input tokens, plus a repeated 301-token request. It recorded
62,050 Host refill misses and 101,299,520 Host-to-device bytes. Both
Decode ranks mapped the same 1 GiB Host backing. A separate earlier
pairing also matched these cases with `FULL_DECODE_ONLY` and capture
size 1.

## Scope and qualification

This PR covers bulk Pull. AscendStore pooling and layerwise transfer are
outside its scope. Shared Host allocation requires a single Decode node
with multiprocessing and PP=PCP=DCP=1. The results above are tied to
their tested revisions and configurations. The current Core pairing
still needs end-to-end NPU qualification.

AI assistance was used for implementation, investigation, tests and this
description.

#23362 upgraded the base image from CANN 9.3.0 to `9.3.0_20261125184600`

targets. It affects all platforms and all Nightly jobs.

After #23362, Nightly on commit `97af565` showed broad failures across
platforms:

- A2: Qwen3-30B-A3B BF16/W8A8 performance below `0.97 * baseline`.
- A3: multiple PD multi-node cases failed (`test_multi_node`,
AssertionError / RuntimeError).
- A5: server startup `RuntimeError` and one job exceeded the `2h` limit.
- A3 logs were masked by `obsutil Upload failed (Succeed 0 / Failed 2)`.

The failure window matches the merge of #23362, and the impact spans all
platforms, so a revert is the fastest way to restore a comparable
baseline.

Note: the OpenEuler image build failure caused by yum is not the cause
of these failures. Nightly tests use the Ubuntu images.

Revert the full `e1c87bfda`, including:

- `Dockerfile`, `Dockerfile.a3`, `Dockerfile.a5`, `Dockerfile.310p`, and

- `.github/workflows/scripts/runner_label.json`

[Refactor] Remove remaining Model Runner V1 EPLB implementation (#22244)

### What this PR does / why we need it?

Main removed Model Runner V1, but its EPLB implementation and
shared-component branches remain. This PR removes that dependency chain
while retaining the supported V2 execution path:

- Delete `vllm_ascend/eplb`, its policies, adaptor, updater, transfer
worker, and dedicated tests/examples.
- Remove the non-daemon executor patch, dedicated process group/HCCL
setting, metric hooks, NetLoader layer-registry cleanup and legacy V1
bypass fallback, expert-offload V1 `dynamic_eplb` check, collection
state, static-map loading, and legacy quant-method branches.
- Remove V1/V2 EPLB gates and the retired runner marker from shared MoE
execution, router construction, warmup registration, quant methods,
validation, and initial-layout patch consumers. Initial replica
placement and checkpoint loading still obtain the actual EP size.
- Remove the unused `MoeRouterInput.log2phy` field and the redundant
cross-layer `dynamic_eplb` flag from `MoEFusedExpertsInput`,
`build_fused_experts_input`, and `MoEMlpComputeInput` (quantization
methods read their own `self.use_expert_weight_list` directly for
persistent EPLB/MegaMoe weight lists, W8A8/W8A8FP8 kernel selection, and
quantized MoE LoRA validation). V2 keeps its upstream expert map,
router-state mapping, load recording, expert-weight views, and placement
updates.
- Drop ignored V1 controls from launch configurations while preserving
their effective V2 EPLB settings. This cleanup does not enable EPLB, add
redundant slots, or choose a new load window/step interval for those
launchers. Existing explicit V2 EPLB E2E scenarios remain enabled.
- Clean test names/tags, regenerate the coverage report, and update
current documentation, translations, architecture context, and
CODEOWNERS entries (including adding `@freyfwt` as co-owner for
`/vllm_ascend/ops/fused_moe` and the MoE patch modules). Historical
release notes are unchanged.

The V2 runner/controller, distributed EPLB state/policies/communicators,
routing operators, and Triton kernels are unchanged. The PCP draft
helper changes only its docstring. MXFP8 selects persistent EPLB lists
in its quant-method weight accessors via `self.use_expert_weight_list`,
and the extended test verifies those lists reach the actual GMM hook.

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

Yes. Remove the retired V1 EPLB package, controls (`DYNAMIC_EPLB`,
`EXPERT_MAP_RECORD`, and legacy `additional_config.eplb_config` fields),
and `eplb:*` MS Service Metrics. Configure EPLB with `--enable-eplb` and
`--eplb-config`; Ascend additional configuration retains
`load_collection_phase` and `stair_config`. Release-note fragment:
`release_notes/fragments/22244.yaml`.

Update the existing DeepSeek V4.1 Flash 950DT DP8/TP1 Prefill and Decode
recipes, including the Memcache variant, with the maintained external DP
launcher, MegaMoE shared-expert fusion, and the V2 KV-transfer
connector.
